gaps.statement: The row's own identity field is event_id, so the subject the row reports is an occurrence. The bound history profile state-version declares ontology_roles.event empty, the accepted population surface admits the entities and relations families only, and the accepted ontology therefore declares no Event type. The occurrence e27 carries no record.

The value Pack Shipment classifies the occurrence this row reports. The row's own identity field is event_id, so the subject the row reports is an occurrence. The bound history profile state-version declares ontology_roles.event empty, the accepted population surface admits the entities and relations families only, and the accepted ontology therefore declares no Event type. The occurrence e27 carries no record. Attaching the classification to order:O1 or actor:R4 instead would assert that the order or the party is the activity, which the source does not state.

The value 07-05 17:00 is the time of the occurrence this row reports. The row's own identity field is event_id, so the subject the row reports is an occurrence. The bound history profile state-version declares ontology_roles.event empty, the accepted population surface admits the entities and relations families only, and the accepted ontology therefore declares no Event type. The occurrence e27 carries no record. The value is separately unrepresentable: it states a month, a day, an hour and a minute, and no year and no zone, so no datetime slot in the accepted population surface could carry it even if an occurrence type were admitted, and supplying a year would be invention.

The identifier X1 is also the value of inventory_unit_id in the inventory source, but the field here is named items, which names no concept any declared source defines, so treating the token match as identity is an assumption the bytes do not carry. Typing it under a separate item type would collide with the InventoryUnit record inventory-unit:X1 on one identifier, and one record carries one type.
The identifier X2 is named only here, as an element of the items list. No declared source states what an item is or gives this identifier a type, so any type assigned to it would be invented.
The identifier Y1 is named only here, as an element of the items list. No declared source states what an item is or gives this identifier a type, so any type assigned to it would be invented.

Under every reading the bytes permit, the three item identifiers were packed for order O1. No relation record can be written for it: the item identifiers carry no admitted type, so there is no record for an endpoint to name.

The row states that R4 performed the activity it reports and that the activity concerned order O1. The link between the two runs through the occurrence, which the bound profile does not admit. A direct relation between the party and the order would state something the source does not.
